title: Station Siting Planner
creator: Hank Ratzesberger & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: A plan view of a school site with a draggable station, geometrically computed shadow, clearance, surface and sky-view layers, a mast configuration panel, and a scorecard rating all seven measured quantities from one placement.

learningObjectives: Recommend a station location and justify it against all seven exposure requirements.
Identify which exposure requirements conflict with each other.
Explain why the shield must not sit above the solar sensor.
Explain why a seismometer cannot share the mast.
prerequisites: Chapter 6 radiation shields; Chapter 9 albedo; Chapter 11 seismic mounting

keyQuestions: Where on this site can all seven sensors be well exposed at once?
What does the four-times-height rule actually rule out?
Why is the best-exposed spot the hardest one to power?
What is the mast doing to your accelerometer?
commonMisconceptions: A convenient location near power is good enough.
Shade is only a problem in summer.
One location can be optimal for every sensor without compromise.
An accelerometer can be mounted anywhere on the station.
assessmentOpportunities: Records all seven scores for each candidate and names the trade in each.
Finds an all-good placement unaided and explains what makes it work.
Creates and then resolves the shield-over-solar shadow.
